q: 1. The method of surveying used for determining the relative height of points on the surface of the earth is called ...............
explain: Leveling is the branch of surveying used to determine the relative heights (elevations) of points or objects on the Earth's surface.

q: 2. A surface which is normal to the direction of gravity at all points as indicated by a plumb line is known as ...............
explain: A level surface is a curved surface that is everywhere perpendicular to the direction of gravity (the plumb line).

q: 3. In a closed traverse the algebraic sum of deflection angle is ...............
explain: For a closed traverse, the algebraic sum of the deflection angles must equal 360°.

q: 4. In a precision traverse, included angles are measured by setting the vernier ...............
options: to read zero exactly on back station
to read 5° exactly on back station
somewhere near zero and reading both verniers on back station
explain: In high-precision work, instead of setting to exactly zero, it's better to read the actual initial readings on both verniers to eliminate setting errors.

q: 5. The reduced level of a point on the ground is called ...............
explain: Both 'spot level' and 'spot height' are terms used to describe the elevation (RL) of a specific point on the ground.

q: 6. Local attraction at a place may be due to ...............
explain: Local attraction in magnetic compasses is caused by nearby magnetic materials or electrical currents, such as bare wires carrying electricity.

q: 7. The amount of correction due to local attraction at a place ...............
options: is a constant for all bearings
explain: If a station is affected by local attraction, all bearings taken from that specific station are shifted by the same constant amount.

q: 8. An instrument error in compass survey is because of ...............
options: no counter weight provision to counteract dip
local attraction due to bare current carrying conductors
explain: Instrumental errors are inherent to the device; the lack of a proper counterweight to balance the magnetic dip is a physical flaw of the instrument.

q: 9. The technique of plotting all the accessible stations with a single set up of plane table is called ...............
explain: Radiation is the method where points are located by drawing radial lines from a single instrument station.

q: 10. Radiation plane table survey is the best suited when ...............
explain: Radiation requires measuring the distance from the instrument to the point, making it ideal for short, easily accessible distances.

q: 11. Intersection is preferred to radiation when ...............
options: it is not possible to measure any distance
the points are too far and invisible
explain: The intersection method locates points by the crossing of two rays from different stations, eliminating the need to measure distance to the point physically.

q: 12. The strength of fix is poor when ...............
options: the station is within the great triangle
the station is outside the great circle
the station is within the great circle but outside the great triangle
the station is on the great circle
explain: In the three-point problem, if the instrument station lies on the circumference of the circle passing through the three known points, the position is indeterminate.

q: 13. An advantage of plane tabling is ...............
options: changes to miss details are less
explain: Because plotting happens in the field while looking at the terrain, the surveyor is less likely to omit important details.

q: 14. Which of the following error is not eliminated by the method of repetition of horizontal angle measurement?
options: Error due to eccentricity of verniers
Error due to displacement of station signals
Error due to wrong adjustment of line of collimation and trunnion axis
explain: If the station signal itself has moved or is displaced, repeating the angle measurement from the same (wrong) signal location will not fix the error.

q: 15. Stadia tacheometry was discovered by James Watt in the year ...............
explain: James Watt is credited with the invention of the stadia system for measuring distances in 1770.

q: 16. The diaphragm of a stadia theodolite is fitted with two additional ...............
explain: A stadia diaphragm has the standard crosshairs plus two additional horizontal 'stadia hairs' (one above and one below the center).

q: 17. The staff intercept will be ...............
options: greater farther off the staff is held
smaller, farther off the staff is held
smaller, nearer the staff is held
same, wherever the staff is held
explain: Due to the divergence of the stadia rays, the intercept (difference between top and bottom hair readings) decreases as the staff moves closer to the instrument.

q: 18. One of the tacheometric constants is additive, the other constant, is ...............
explain: The two tacheometric constants are the multiplying constant (k) and the additive constant (c).

q: 19. Tacheometric formula for horizontal distance using horizontal sights can also suitable be employed for inclined sights through θ by multiplying ...............
options: the multiplying constant by cos²θ and additive constant by cos θ
explain: The standard horizontal distance formula for inclined sights is D = ks cos²θ + c cosθ.

q: 20. The image formed by the objective in the plane of cross hairs is ...............
explain: A simple objective lens in a telescope produces a real and inverted image at the focal plane.

q: 21. When the curve is to be set out over a rough ground, the method used is ...............
explain: On rough ground where chaining is difficult, methods that use angles or optical distance measurement (two-theodolite or tacheometric) are preferred.

q: 22. The theodolite method off setting out a curve involves ...............
explain: Theodolite methods (like the two-theodolite method) primarily rely on angular observations to define points on the curve.

q: 23. A curve of varying radius is known as ...............
explain: A transition curve is designed to have a radius that changes continuously (usually from infinity to a fixed radius) to provide a gradual change in centrifugal force.

q: 24. The brightness of the image ............... the magnifying power.
options: varies directly as the square of
varies inversely as the square of
explain: Image brightness is inversely proportional to the square of the magnification because the same amount of light is spread over a larger area.

q: 25. The ratio of the focal length of the objective to that of an eye-piece of a telescope is called its ...............
explain: Magnification (m) = f(objective) / f(eyepiece).

q: 26. When the length of chain used in measuring distance is longer than the standard length, the error in measured distance will be ...............
explain: If the chain is too long, it measures a shorter distance than actual, resulting in a negative error (Correction is positive).

q: 27. Overturning of vehicles on a curve can be avoided by using ...............
explain: Transition curves allow for the gradual introduction of super-elevation, which helps counter centrifugal force and prevent overturning.

q: 28. The rise and fall method ...............
options: is less accurate than height of instrument method
is not suitable for leveling with tilting levels
provides a check on the reduction of intermediate point levels
quicker and less tedious for large number of intermediate sights
explain: Unlike the HI method, the Rise and Fall method includes a calculation check for every single intermediate sight.

q: 29. If the staff is not held vertical at a leveling station, the reduced level calculated from the observation would be ...............
explain: An inclined staff always results in a reading higher than the true vertical reading, which makes the calculated RL lower than the actual RL.

q: 30. "Cross-section" and "Longitudinal sectioning" is ...............
explain: Profile leveling is used to determine the elevations of points along a fixed line (longitudinal) and perpendicular to it (cross-section).

q: 31. Height of instrument method of booking readings is adopted ...............
options: when less number of intermediate sights exist
explain: In profile leveling, where there are many intermediate sights, the HI method is much faster than the Rise and Fall method.

q: 32. An invert is taken when the point is ...............
explain: An invert level reading is taken by holding the staff upside down against the ceiling or soffit of a structure located above the instrument's line of sight.

q: 33. In survey it was recorded that ΣRise = 0, then ...............
options: the survey had many invert readings
explain: If the sum of rises is zero, it implies there were no falls recorded, which indicates a continuously rising ground profile.

q: 34. When the staff is held on a B.M. of R.L. 100.000, the staff reading was 2.000. When the staff is held on station P, the reading was 3.000. Hence height of the instrument is ...............
explain: Height of Instrument (HI) = RL of Bench Mark + Back Sight = 100.000 + 2.000 = 102.000.

q: 35. At the magnetic poles, the amount of dip is ...............
explain: At the magnetic poles, the magnetic lines of force are vertical, so the dip is 90°.

q: 36. The lines of earth's magnetic field run from ...............
explain: Magnetic field lines traditionally run from the North magnetic pole to the South magnetic pole.

q: 37. The ratio of the angles subtended at the eye, by the virtual image and the object, is known as telescope's ...............
explain: This is the angular magnification, the ratio of the angle subtended by the image to the angle subtended by the object.

q: 38. A bearing of a line is also known as ...............
explain: The 'true bearing' of a line is its orientation relative to the geographical North, often referred to as the azimuth in general contexts.

q: 39. ABCD is a rectangular plot of land. If the bearing of the side AB is 75°, the bearing of DC is ...............
explain: In a rectangle ABCD, side AB is parallel to DC. Parallel lines have the same bearing in the same direction.

q: 40. Back bearing of a line is equal to ...............
explain: Back Bearing = Fore Bearing ± 180° (use + if FB < 180°, and - if FB > 180°).

q: 41. The magnetic bearing of a line is 32° and the magnetic declination is 10°15'W. The true bearing is ...............
explain: True Bearing = Magnetic Bearing - West Declination = 32°00' - 10°15' = 21°45'.

q: 42. The magnetic meridian at any point, is the direction indicated by a freely suspended ...............
options: properly balanced and uninfluenced by local attractive
magnetic needle over an iron pivot
explain: To accurately show the meridian, the needle must be balanced and free from outside magnetic interference (local attraction).

q: 43. The horizontal angle between true meridian and magnetic meridian, is known ...............
explain: The horizontal angle between true North and magnetic North is called magnetic declination.

q: 44. Setting out of a simple curve by two theodolite method does not require ...............
explain: The two-theodolite method allows for curve setting using only angular intersection, meaning no chaining (linear measurement) along the curve is needed.

q: 45. In a reverse curve, the super elevation provided at the point of reverse curvature is ...............
options: dependent on the element of reverse curve
explain: At the point of reverse curvature, the direction of curvature changes; therefore, the super-elevation must pass through zero as it switches sides.

q: 46. Short offsets are measured with ...............
explain: Ordinary chains are standard for taking short offsets in general chain surveying.

q: 47. Greater accuracy in linear measurements, is obtained by ...............
explain: Invar tapes have a very low coefficient of thermal expansion, making them the most accurate for baseline measurements.

q: 48. It is more difficult to obtain good results while measuring horizontal distance by stepping ...............
explain: Stepping uphill is harder because the person at the front must maintain alignment and plumbing while looking 'up' the slope.

q: 49. θ1 and θ2 are the angles of elevation from A to the top and bottom of vertically held rod of length S at B. The horizontal distance AB is ...............
explain: Using trigonometry: h1 = D tan θ1 and h2 = D tan θ2. The length S = h1 - h2 = D(tan θ1 - tan θ2), so D = S/(tan θ1 - tan θ2).

q: 50. Subtense tacheometry is generally preferred to if ground is ...............
explain: The subtense bar method is particularly useful in rough or undulating terrain where chaining is difficult or impossible.

q: 51. Different grades are joined together by ...............
explain: A vertical curve is used to provide a smooth transition between two different gradients (grades) on a road or railway.

q: 52. Grid lines are parallel to ...............
options: magnetic meridian of the central point of the grid
line representing the central true meridian of the grid
explain: Grid lines in a coordinate system are typically aligned parallel to the central true meridian of that specific grid zone.

q: 53. The sum of the interior angles of a geometrical figure laid on the surface of the earth differs from that of the corresponding plane figure only to the extent of one second for every ...............
explain: In geodetic surveying, the spherical excess (difference in angles) is 1 second for every 195.5 sq. km of area; since 195.5 is not an option, 'none of these' is selected.

q: 54. In a tacheometer provided with anallactic lens distance between object glass and vertical axis is 15 cm. Focal length of the objective is 15 cm and that of anallactic lens is 10 cm. Hence distance between the two lenses is ...............
explain: For an anallactic lens, the distance between the objective and the anallactic lens (d) is calculated to make the additive constant zero. In this specific configuration, it results in 17.5 cm.

q: 55. When the cross-hairs are not clearly visible ...............
explain: Focusing the eye-piece is specifically done to make the cross-hairs appear distinct and sharp for the observer's vision.

q: 56. Cross staff is an instrument used for ...............
explain: A cross-staff is a simple instrument used in chain surveying to set out perpendicular offsets (right angles) from the chain line.

q: 57. Normal tension is that pull which ...............
options: is used at the time of standardizing the tape
neutralizes the effect due to pull and sag
makes the correction due to sag equal to zero
makes the correction due to pull equal to zero
explain: Normal tension is the specific amount of pull where the positive correction for pull exactly equals the negative correction for sag.

q: 58. Which of the following is not used in measuring perpendicular offsets?
explain: A line ranger is used to establish intermediate points on a straight line, not for measuring perpendicular offsets.

q: 59. Which of the following instrument is generally used for base line measurements?
explain: Invar tapes are used for primary baseline measurements because their low thermal expansion ensures high precision.

q: 60. An invar tape is made of an alloy of ...............
explain: Invar is an alloy consisting of approximately 36% nickel and 64% steel.

q: 61. Ranging is the process of ...............
options: fixing ranging rods on the extremities of area
aligning the chain in a straight line between two extremities
taking offsets from a chain line
chaining over a range of mountains
explain: Ranging is the operation of establishing intermediate points on a straight line between two distant fixed stations.

q: 62. While viewing through a level telescope and moving the eye slightly, a relative movement occurs between the image of the leveling staff and the cross hairs. The instrument is ...............
explain: Parallax occurs when the image formed by the objective does not fall exactly on the plane of the cross-hairs.

q: 63. Diaphragm of a surveying telescope is held inside ...............
options: telescope at the end nearer the eye-piece
explain: The diaphragm containing the cross-hairs is placed in the focal plane of the objective, which is situated just in front of the eye-piece.

q: 64. In leveling operation ...............
options: if second reading is more than first, it represents a rise
if first reading is more than second, it represents a rise
if first reading is less than second, it represents a fall
explain: In leveling, a higher staff reading indicates a lower point (fall), and a lower staff reading indicates a higher point (rise).

q: 65. For the construction of highway (or railway) ...............
options: both longitudinal and cross sections are required
explain: Longitudinal sections are needed for the center-line gradient, and cross-sections are needed to calculate earthwork volumes.

q: 66. An imaginary line joining the points of equal elevation on the surface of the earth, represents ...............
explain: A contour line is a line on a map that connects points of equal elevation above a datum.

q: 67. The boundary of water of a still lake, represents ...............
explain: The shoreline of a still body of water is a natural example of a contour line, as all points on the water surface are at the same elevation.

q: 68. The constant vertical distance between two adjacent contours, is called ...............
explain: Contour interval is the fixed vertical difference in elevation between any two consecutive contour lines.

q: 69. The contour interval is kept inversely proportional to ...............
options: time and expense of field work
steepness of the configuration of the area
explain: On steep ground, contours are close together, so a larger interval is used; on flat ground, a smaller interval is used to show detail.

q: 70. The representation of general topography of a very flat terrain is possible only ...............
options: by drawing contours at large interval
by drawing contours at small interval
by giving spot levels at large interval
by giving spot levels to features at close interval
explain: In very flat areas, contour lines are far apart and provide little detail, so spot levels (specific elevations at certain points) are used instead.

q: 71. Contour interval, within the limits of a map ...............
options: may vary according to the configuration
explain: To avoid confusion and allow for accurate reading of slopes, the contour interval must remain the same throughout a single map.

q: 72. The direction of steepest slope on a contour, is ...............
options: at an angle of 45° to the contour
at right angles to the contour
explain: The shortest distance between two contours (the steepest path) is always the perpendicular distance between them.

q: 73. Straight, parallel and widely spaced contours represent ...............
explain: Parallel and equally spaced straight contours indicate a uniform slope or an inclined plane surface.

q: 74. Two contour lines, having the same may cross each other only in the case of ...............
explain: According to the book's specific logic/key for this question, contours 'can cross' in the specific topographical anomaly of an overhanging cliff.

q: 75. Contours of different elevations may cross each other only in the case of ...............
explain: In an overhanging cliff, a vertical line would pass through two different points of the same surface, causing the contours to appear to cross on a 2D map.

q: 76. Closed contours of decreasing values toward their centre, represent ...............
explain: If the elevation values decrease toward the center of closed loops, it indicates a hole, pond, or depression in the ground.

q: 77. The Simpson's rule of areas assumes that the portions of the boundary between the ends of ordinates are ...............
explain: Simpson's rule (Prismoidal rule) is based on the assumption that the boundary is a second-degree curve (parabola).

q: 78. The difference between the sum of the angles of a spherical triangle on the earth's surface and the angles of the corresponding plane triangle for every 195.5 km² of area is only ...............
explain: This is the definition of spherical excess for a triangle on the Earth's surface: 1 second per 195.5 sq. km.

q: 79. In order to determine the natural features such as valleys, rivers, lakes etc., the surveying preferred is ...............
explain: Topographical surveys are conducted to map the physical natural features of the land along with man-made objects.

q: 80. The surveying used to determine additional details such as boundaries of fields, is called ...............
explain: Cadastral surveys are specifically used to establish or re-establish property boundaries and for legal land ownership purposes.

q: 81. The fundamental principle of surveying is to work from the ...............
explain: Working from 'whole to part' prevents the accumulation of errors by localizing them within small areas.

q: 82. The working from whole to the part is done in surveying in order to ensure that ...............
options: surveying work is completed more quickly
errors and mistakes of one portion do not affected the remaining portion
explain: By establishing a primary control network first, any errors in detail surveying are confined and do not spread through the whole project.

q: 83. The theodolites used for making tacheometric observations by optical wedge system, are ...............
options: provided with stadia hairs in front of eye piece
not provided with stadia hairs at all
fitted with a glass wedge inside the telescope
fitted with a glass wedge in front of telescope
explain: The optical wedge system involves placing a glass wedge in front of half the objective to create a fixed displacement for distance measurement.

q: 84. The curve composed of two arcs of different radii having their centers on the opposite side of the curve, is known ...............
explain: A reverse curve (S-curve) consists of two circular arcs bending in opposite directions with centers on opposite sides of the common tangent.

q: 85. Ceylon Ghat tracer can read slopes up to ...............
explain: The Ceylon Ghat Tracer is a simple instrument used for setting out gradients, typically ranging from 1 in 6 to 1 in 120.

q: 86. The horizon glass of the box sextant is ...............
options: concave in shape to from sharp image
explain: The horizon glass is half-silvered to allow the observer to see the horizon directly through the clear part and the reflected object in the silvered part.

q: 87. If the angle between index glass and horizon glasses of a box sextant is 40° the horizontal angle between A and B sight by it is ...............
explain: In reflecting instruments, the angle between the objects is twice the angle between the mirrors. 40° x 2 = 80°.

q: 88. An open cross-staff is commonly used for setting out ...............
explain: While cross-staffs are for right angles, the 'open' type is often utilized for relatively longer offsets compared to simple chain offsets.

q: 89. The angle of intersection of the horizon glass and index glass in an optical square is ...............
explain: The two mirrors of an optical square are fixed at an angle of 45° to reflect rays through 90°.

q: 90. The horizontal glass in an optical square is ...............
options: one-fourth silvered and half un silvered
half silvered and half un silvered
explain: The horizon glass is half-silvered so the observer can see one signal directly and the other by reflection.

q: 91. The index glass in an optical square is ...............
options: one-fourth silvered and half un silvered
half silvered and half un silvered
explain: The index glass is completely silvered to ensure a strong reflection of the object onto the horizon glass.

q: 92. The instrument, belonging to a class of reflecting instrument is ...............
explain: All these instruments use the principles of reflection (mirrors or prisms) to align sights or read scales.

q: 93. In an optical square, the angle between the first incident ray and the last reflected ray is ...............
explain: The geometry of an optical square is specifically designed to result in a 90° deviation between the original ray and the final reflected ray.

q: 94. When the object lies on the left hand side of the chain line, then while taking offset with an optical square, it is held in ...............
explain: To view an object on the left through the reflection while staying on the line, holding it upright in the right hand is the standard procedure.

q: 95. The suitable contour interval for a map with scale 1:10000 is ...............
explain: A common rule for contour interval is 25 / (number of cm per km). For 1:10000 (10 cm = 1 km), it would be 2.5m, so 2m is the closest standard interval.

q: 96. Check lines (or proof lines) in Chain Surveying are essentially required ...............
options: to indicate the accuracy of the survey work
explain: Check lines are measured to verify the accuracy of the framework and plotting; if the check line distance matches the plot, the work is correct.

q: 97. A well conditioned triangle has no angle less than ...............
explain: A triangle is well-conditioned if its angles are between 30° and 120° to ensure accurate intersection points.

q: 98. Point of tangency is the ...............
options: common point where the radius changes
common point where the radius and direction changes
explain: The Point of Curve (PC) is the start, and the Point of Tangency (PT) is the end of the curve where it joins the forward tangent.

q: 99. In a simple curve, 'External distance' is the distance between ...............
options: vertex and middle point of the curve
vertex and the centre of the curve
point of curve and point of tangency
explain: The external distance (apex distance) is the distance from the intersection point (vertex) to the apex of the curve.

q: 100. An instrument used to find slopes of ground is ...............
explain: A clinometer is specifically designed to measure angles of slope, elevation, or depression.
